Donald Glover to Write, Direct and Star in Netflix’s Live‑Action PUBG Series

Netflix Announces a PUBG Adaptation

Krafton, the South‑Korean publisher behind the battle‑royale hit *PlayerUnknown’s Battlegrounds* (PUBG), confirmed that a live‑action television series based on the game is in development for Netflix. The project will be written, directed and led on‑screen by Grammy‑winning artist and actor Donald Glover, with his brother Stephen Glover serving as co‑writer and executive producer.

Creative Team and Production Partners

The series’ executive‑producer roster includes:

  • Michael Schaefer (Neon TV)
  • Fam Udeorji (Gilga)
  • Taeseok Jang and Sujin Lee (LV3H)

LV3H is Krafton’s own entertainment division, which is also credited with developing and producing the show. The involvement of multiple production houses suggests a sizable budget and a collaborative approach to adapting the game’s world for television.

What the Game’s Lore Offers

While PUBG originated as a pure multiplayer shooter, Krafton has expanded its universe with a narrative that can be accessed on the official PUBG website. According to that lore, the titular Battlegrounds were conceived by a billionaire named Sergei Kalimnik, a survivor of a 1965 Soviet attack on the fictional island of Erangel. After enduring 17 days of conflict and witnessing the disposal of bodies by Soviet officials, Kalimnik purchased the island and instituted a deadly contest that forces 100 participants to fight until only one remains. The backstory links the modern Battlegrounds to a historic tradition called *Magna Venari* (“The Great Hunt”), a 15th‑century practice of hunting human prey to explore why some survive while others do not. This mythic framing provides a narrative scaffolding that Glover can draw upon, moving the adaptation beyond a straightforward tournament‑style plot.

Practical Implications for Fans and the Industry

  • For PUBG players: The series could broaden the game’s audience, potentially driving new player sign‑ups and increasing in‑game revenue. However, the show’s tone and focus may differ from the fast‑paced multiplayer experience, so expectations should be managed.
  • For Netflix: Adding a high‑profile gaming IP aligns with the streamer’s strategy of diversifying content. The involvement of a well‑known creator like Glover may attract viewers who are unfamiliar with PUBG but follow his previous work (*Atlanta*, *Community*).
  • For the broader adaptation market: PUBG joins a growing list of video‑game properties receiving live‑action treatment, following titles such as *The Witcher* and upcoming projects like Michael B. Jordan’s *Battlefield* film. Success or failure could influence future green‑lighting decisions for similar adaptations.

How Readers Can Verify the Announcement

The information comes from an official press release shared with IGN, which can be accessed at the following URL: https://www.ign.com/articles/pubg-is-getting-a-live-action-series-on-netflix-written-directed-by-and-starring-donald-glover Readers can cross‑check the details by visiting Krafton’s newsroom or Netflix’s press site for any subsequent statements.

Outlook

Donald Glover’s track record of blending humor, social commentary, and genre‑bending storytelling suggests the PUBG series could offer a fresh take on the battle‑royale concept, potentially exploring the darker themes hinted at in the game’s expanded lore. Until more specifics are released—such as a trailer, casting announcements beyond the Glover brothers, or a premiere window—fans should treat the current details as the definitive, verified foundation of the project.
